text.12_Arrogance and Humility, 6_Paragraph: To cancel the arrogance which it a form of idol-worship. The importance is to get closer of the Tzaddikim (Ibid. 5). [en]
text.12_Arrogance and Humility, 7_Paragraph: Pour annuler l'orgueil qui est une forme d'idolâtrie. L'essentiel est de se rapprocher des Tzaddikim (ibid. 5). [fr]
text.25_Anger, 9_Paragraph: Anger harms one’s livelihood, as mentioned above. As a result, a person becomes distanced from truth, and because of this, he is unable to pray. Additionally, he cannot fully bring into action what he needs to accomplish. (Likutey Moharan I, 66:2)
text.48_Torah Learning, 27_Paragraph: Through Torah and prayer, one merits joy. Through joy, one merits holy boldness. Through holy boldness, one merits drawing close to true tzaddikim (righteous individuals). Through them, one merits perfect faith. Through faith, one attains the aspect of "hands"—the ability to accept reproof from true rebukers. This, in turn, saves one from exile and conflict, increasing peace in the world and establishing peace between Israel and their Father in Heaven. At that point, one rectifies and seals holiness with the concept of a "seal within a seal." (Likutei Moharan I, Torah 22:9)
